whitespace_angles.angle: Pre-intent commerce: surfacing products before users form a query
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Every major publication covers agentic commerce as pull-based — user opens ChatGPT/Perplexity and asks. Nobody has published the counterargument that the most powerful commerce surface is pre-intent: before the user decides to shop. Glance's D0 feed operates in this window at scale across 175M devices.

whitespace_angles.angle: OEM-level AI as a trust layer that app stores cannot replicate
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Stratechery and The Agentic Commerce Frontier both cover UCP and ACP protocols (Google/OpenAI respectively) but treat OEM-embedded surfaces as an afterthought. No one has written about OEM pre-consent — how Glance bypasses app-install friction by being baked into the OS layer at the factory.

whitespace_angles.angle: The D0 activation window as a measurable commerce category
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Commerce content universally frames the funnel as starting at search or app-open. The window between device wake and first app-open (D0) is unaddressed in any major publication. Glance can coin and own this category with device-scale data.

whitespace_angles.angle: Multi-agent orchestration for passive personalisation (vs. active instruction)
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Coverage of multi-agent systems focuses on task automation (book a flight, buy a product on command). The Glance architecture — 5 passive sub-agents (Weather, Trends, Occasion, Physical Stylist, Lifestyle Detective) that run without user instruction — is architecturally distinct and uncovered.

whitespace_angles.angle: What UCP and ACP miss: commerce without a session
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Both Google's Universal Commerce Protocol and OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol assume a user-initiated session. Lockscreen commerce has no session — only ambient signal. Glance is the only scaled platform that can write this counterpoint with real data.

whitespace_angles.angle: Virtual try-on as infrastructure, not a feature
whitespace_angles.why_glance: Google's Doppl shutdown and VTON integration into Search has been covered as a feature story. Nobody has written the infrastructure argument: that VTON is a conversion layer that belongs to whoever controls the surface seen first. Glance surfaces it on the lockscreen before Search.

momentum_angles.angle: Agentic checkout and autonomous purchase completion
momentum_angles.coverage_summary: Stripe Sessions launch (288 products), UCP protocol rollout, and Amazon vs. Perplexity legal battle are driving heavy coverage of who controls the checkout layer in agentic commerce.
momentum_angles.glance_counter_angle: Checkout is the last mile. Glance owns the first mile — discovery that happens before users form purchase intent. The checkout protocol war matters less if the discovery surface is owned.

momentum_angles.angle: Protocol wars: Google UCP vs. OpenAI ACP
momentum_angles.coverage_summary: Ben Thompson's 'Apple and Gemini, Foundation vs. Aggregation, Universal Commerce Protocol' piece framed UCP as Google running its classic playbook. OpenAI's ACP is positioned as the challenger. Both require app-open to function.
momentum_angles.glance_counter_angle: Glance doesn't need either protocol at the discovery layer. The lockscreen surface operates upstream of both UCP and ACP sessions.

momentum_angles.coverage_summary: Debra Williamson and Andrew Lipsman are pushing back on inflated AI commerce stats — Adobe's 693% Gen AI traffic spike is actually 0.1% to 0.6% of total traffic. Reality-check framing is gaining traction.
momentum_angles.glance_counter_angle: Glance can lead a data-backed counter: 175M pre-installed devices isn't a traffic spike, it's structural distribution. The distinction between pull AI (ChatGPT shopping) and push AI (D0 lockscreen) sidesteps the hype critique entirely.

per_publication_summary.name: The Agentic Commerce Frontier
per_publication_summary.recent_focus: Infrastructure standardization (UCP, ACP), payment authorization for AI agents, merchant tooling, Wayfair's multi-platform strategy
per_publication_summary.notable_post: Apr 21–26 issue: deep-dive on how payment networks (Stripe, Amex, Visa) are preparing for agent-mediated purchases at scale
per_publication_summary.gap_vs_glance: Covers merchant-side and protocol-side extensively. Zero coverage of OEM-embedded surfaces, lockscreen discovery, or pre-intent commerce.

per_publication_summary.name: AI Ad Economy (Debra Williamson / Andrew Lipsman)
per_publication_summary.recent_focus: Reality-checking agentic commerce claims, retail media threat analysis, ad measurement in AI surfaces
per_publication_summary.notable_post: Agentic Commerce Reality Check: debunks Adobe 693% Gen AI traffic stat as misleading (0.1% → 0.6% share)
per_publication_summary.gap_vs_glance: Strong on measurement critique but no coverage of ambient/passive surfaces. Glance's pre-install distribution doesn't fit the 'traffic spike' narrative they're critiquing.

per_publication_summary.name: Stratechery (Ben Thompson)
per_publication_summary.recent_focus: Aggregation theory in the AI era, Google UCP as classic aggregator playbook, Apple + Gemini tensions, opportunity cost of compute
per_publication_summary.notable_post: 'Apple and Gemini, Foundation vs. Aggregation, Universal Commerce Protocol' — frames UCP as Google's attempt to extend aggregation to agentic era
per_publication_summary.gap_vs_glance: Thompson's aggregation theory framework is perfect for a Glance counterpoint: OEM pre-install is a different aggregation vector than search or app stores — one Thompson has never addressed.

per_publication_summary.name: Lenny's Newsletter
per_publication_summary.recent_focus: AI product growth playbooks, team structure for AI companies, the new growth loops in 0-to-1 AI products
per_publication_summary.notable_post: Elena Verna on Lovable hitting $200M ARR with 100 employees — the new AI growth playbook
per_publication_summary.gap_vs_glance: GTM and growth content for SaaS/app companies. No coverage of hardware/OEM distribution as a growth channel or the lockscreen as a product surface.

per_publication_summary.name: Fast Company
per_publication_summary.recent_focus: Google/OpenAI race for agentic commerce, 'Shop til you bot' framing of autonomous shopping agents
per_publication_summary.notable_post: 'Shop til you bot: Google, OpenAI, and the race to build agentic commerce' — overview of competing protocols
per_publication_summary.gap_vs_glance: Frames the race as Google vs. OpenAI. Glance is the third competitor that neither protocol covers: embedded, pre-intent, OEM-distributed.
